chapters.title: Same room, or a phone call

scenes.narration: Two settings in your server look like performance tuning. One of them silently switches off sampling.
MCP messages are just JSON. How they travel is a separate decision, and it's a decision with consequences. Learn MCP, on THE NBX STUDIO.

scenes.headline: Same room, or [a phone call]
scenes.caption: two transports
scenes.premise: Both move identical JSON. The only difference is whether the two programs share a machine.
scenes.narration: There are two transports worth knowing, and they carry exactly the same JSON. ^Stdio means the client launches the server as a child process on the same machine and they talk over standard input and standard output — like two people at one desk passing notes. Every feature works, setup is nothing, and it only ever works locally. ^Streamable H T T P means the server runs somewhere else entirely and you reach it over the network, which is what you need the moment the server isn't on the user's laptop. That's the whole choice: stdio while you're developing, H T T P when you ship.

scenes.headline: What the flags [turn off]
scenes.caption: read this twice
scenes.premise: Both flags are passed to run(), not to the constructor. Both trade features for scale, and nothing warns you.
scenes.narration: Now the trap, and it's worth reading twice. |First, where these flags actually live, because this catches anyone who learnt MCP a year ago: they are not constructor arguments. |You pass them to run, alongside the transport, and the server object itself knows nothing about them. |Stateless h t t p true means the server forgets each client between requests, ^which is exactly what you want behind a load balancer, because any instance can then answer any request. The cost is severe, though: sampling stops working, elicitation stops working, roots stop working, and subscriptions stop working — every one of those needs the server to remember who you are between calls. |Json response true means replies come back as plain JSON instead of a stream, ^which kills live progress and log messages, since streaming is the mechanism those travel on. ^Notice what survives both: ordinary tool calls. So start with both false, which is the default, and only reach for either when you genuinely need horizontal scaling and can say out loud what you're giving up.

lines.detail: The constructor takes no transport flags.
They belong to run(), with the transport.
Scales. Kills sampling, elicitation, roots, subscriptions.
Simpler. Kills streaming progress and log messages.
